messages:
vendor_accounting: Hi team — we received invoice `2026-INV-1893` but it shows VAT charged. Our EU branch (NL) should be reverse-charge. Can you reissue with reverse-charge notation and our VAT ID? Also flag: our local team asked if Redwood can gross-up for any withholding — contract mention. Need confirmation ASAP, payment deadline approaching.

jess_finance: Thanks — can you paste the full VAT ID and the billing country? Also can you attach the PO/contract clause that supports reverse-charge? We need that to reissue.

matt_tax: Quick tax note: reverse-charge applies B2B intra-EU when the buyer is VAT-registered and provides a valid VAT number. W-8/W-9 are US docs (not relevant here) unless vendor also has a US entity. If vendor asks for gross-up for local withholding, we need a contract clause authorizing it or a tax residency certificate (TRC) to determine withholding relief.

vendor_accounting: VAT ID: `NL812345678B01`. Billing country: Netherlands (buyer is our NL branch). Attached: screenshot of our billing profile + excerpt of contract (see drive link). We do have clause that mentions gross-up for withholding but it's ambiguous about amounts. Link: https://drive.internal/vendor/contract/abc123 (placeholder).

ana_ops: @legal_team FYI — vendor sent contract excerpt to drive. Can legal confirm whether clause supports 10% gross-up request?

liam_sales: The product is SaaS, should be zero-rated under reverse-charge when buyer is VAT-registered. We should avoid charging VAT if docs are clean. Hold payment until reissue to avoid messy reclaim.

legal_team: Reviewing clause 6.2 now. Initial read: clause allows "tax gross-up" only where explicitly stated and limited to statutory withholding rates up to 5% with prior written approval. Vendor's ask for 10% looks outside that. We can approve reissue with reverse-charge notation; we will not approve a 10% gross-up without contractual amendment. Please request TRC if they claim relief.

jess_finance: Understood. @matt_tax can you confirm the calculation approach if we were to gross-up? Provide formula so we can show the vendor, but don't approve yet.

matt_tax: Formula (for reference): `gross = net / (1 - wht_rate)` e.g., for 10%: `gross = net / 0.9`. But per legal, we don't have authority to gross-up to 10% here. Alternative: vendor provides TRC and we pay gross amount and refund WHT after relief, or we withhold at source following local law.

jess_finance: OK — action items: 1) reissue invoice with reverse-charge and vendor VAT ID 2) do not gross-up 3) request TRC for any WHT relief 4) hold payment until vendor confirms or provides TRC. @billing-bot please queue reissue with reference to original invoice.

billing-bot: Reissue queued: original `2026-INV-1893` -> new draft `2026-INV-1893-RC` (job id 2332100050). ETA ~15m. Payment hold flag set.

vendor_accounting: Thanks — we'll send TRC if possible. Can you confirm the exact wording you'd add for reverse-charge? Need to update our records.

jess_finance: We'll add: "Reverse charge — VAT to be accounted for by the customer under Article 194 (EU VAT Directive). Customer VAT ID: NL812345678B01." Also include our billing contact and mention debit note will be reissued if needed.

liam_sales: :thumbsup: Keep me posted. We want to avoid delaying onboarding.

billing-bot: Invoice reissued and emailed to vendor_alternative@example.com. New invoice id `2026-INV-1893-RC`. Payment hold remains until TRC received or vendor confirms no WHT applies.

vendor_accounting: Received, thanks. We'll try to provide TRC in 2 business days. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

jess_finance: Great — closing loop for now. If legal/matt want to change approach after seeing TRC, we'll reopen.
